name: Measuring tape
lead: A flexible measuring tape is a ribbon of cloth or plastic with a marked scale, used to measure circumferences such as waist, chest, arms and thighs.
In physique tracking it provides a cheap check on body composition changes that the scale misses: a shrinking waist with a stable or growing chest and arm indicates recomposition.

paras: A tape records the girth of a body segment at a fixed landmark. Changes in waist circumference track abdominal fat changes, and growth in limb circumference tracks muscle gain, when taken at consistent sites, times and tension. There is no gadget-specific research; its usefulness follows from the established use of anthropometry in nutrition and health research.

The method is operator dependent: tape height, tension, breathing and posture shift the result by centimeters, and daily fluctuation from food and water is common. It tells you nothing about composition by itself. Obsessive daily measuring can feed body-image anxiety, so weekly measurements at the same time are sensible.
